data.name: Chidghana
data.long_meaning: The name Chidghana is derived from Sanskrit words Chid (wealth) and Ghana (Lord). This name is dedicated to the Lord of Wealth and Prosperity, symbolizing abundance, richness, and material success.
data.spiritual_meaning: Invokes blessings of the Lord of Wealth for material prosperity and spiritual growth.
data.numerology_meaning: People with this name are nurturing, loving, and committed. They have a strong desire to help others and are often seen as caretakers. They are also highly intuitive and can sense the emotions of others.

data.cultural_impact: The name Chidghana is rooted in the sacred Hindu traditions and carries significant cultural significance. The word Chid symbolizes wealth, prosperity, and happiness, while Ghana stands for the divine Lord who is believed to bestow these blessings. The name signifies the pursuit of material success, which is an essential part of the Hindu paradigm and can be seen in the importance placed on prosperity and abundance in various aspects of Hindu life, from religious rituals to social and economic institutions.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeper spiritual level, the name Chidghana challenges us to understand the true nature of wealth and prosperity. The name reminds us that true wealth does not lie in material possessions, but in the inner richness and abundance that comes from being in a state of peace, contentment, and connection to the divine. By invoking the blessings of the Lord of Wealth, this name also serves as a reminder to cultivate generosity, humility, and gratitude in our lives, recognizing that all blessings come from a higher power and should be shared with others. Ultimately, Chidghana encourages us to seek and cherish both the material and spiritual dimensions of life, recognizing the interconnectedness and interdependence of all things.

historical_references.reference: Chidghana was a ruler of the Chidambara Nataraja temple in Tamil Nadu, India, during the Chola period. He is mentioned in the Tirumurai, a collection of hymns composed by the Tamil Saiva Saints.
historical_references.context: Temple administration and Saiva Saint hymns

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Chidghana comes from the Brihadeeswarar Temple inscription, which mentions him as a royal donor during the reign of Rajaraja Chola I (1014-1044 CE).
